column1: # JavaScript definitions. Rule, in addition to function and class declarations, methods, and `const f = () => {}` / `= function () {}` bindings at any depth:

#  - CommonJS: `exports.x = function` / `module.exports.x = function` at the top of the file define the function x (class x for a class); the name is the property, not the function expression's own name;

#  - `module.exports = function createApp() {}` defines createApp; an anonymous function, arrow or class there is named after the file (merge-options.js is mergeOptions, widget/index.js is widget); the entries of a top-level `module.exports = { ... }` are definitions when they are methods or hold a function;
#  - `Foo.prototype.bar = function` defines the method bar owned by Foo, wherever it is written; `function Foo` is then a class;

#  - `obj.name = function` is the method name owned by obj only as a top-level statement on an object the same file declares at its top level; inside a function, on `this`, or on an undeclared object it is an assignment and defines nothing;

#  - `export const/let/var x = value` is a constant (variable for let and var); createContext(...) is a constant, exported or not; a component built by memo, forwardRef, lazy, observer, defineComponent or styled is a function; `const X = class {}` is a class;
#  - a constant that is not exported, a call result that is not one of those, and an assignment that aliases another name (`exports.alias = exports.parse`) are not definitions.
#  - a private `#name` method is a method and a private `#name` class field a field, named with the `#`; a public class field is not a definition.
